subject: science
passage: An octopus has roughly 500 million neurons, but about two-thirds of them lie not in its brain but in its eight arms. An arm can still touch, taste, and grasp food even after it has been separated from the body. For neurobiologist Ilse Vandermeer, this distribution implies a striking division of labor: the central brain issues only broad commands, such as "reach toward that crab," and leaves the arms to work out every detail of a movement for themselves.
passage_b: Octopus arms are undeniably capable of acting on their own, but that capacity does not show that they always do. In one experiment, octopuses learned to steer a single arm through a transparent maze toward food that they could see but that the arm could not reach by touch or taste until the very end. Because the arm's own senses offered no guide to the route, success depended on the brain watching the arm and correcting its path along the way.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim about the central brain in Text 1?

choices.A: By suggesting that octopus arms actually contain far fewer neurons than Text 1 indicates
choices.B: By claiming that in the maze experiment the arm, not the brain, worked out the route
choices.C: By rejecting the idea that an octopus's arms can sense and respond to their surroundings
choices.D: By arguing that it overlooks cases in which the brain guides an arm's movements closely

explanation.why: Text 1 says the brain issues "only broad commands" and leaves "every detail" to the arms. Text 2 grants that arms can act on their own but describes a maze task in which "success depended on the brain watching the arm and correcting its path." So Text 2 would say Text 1's claim misses cases of close central control.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 never discusses how many neurons the arms contain.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This reverses Text 2's point: the arm's senses "offered no guide to the route," so the brain had to guide it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 calls the arms "undeniably capable of acting on their own," so it does not reject their ability to sense and respond.
explanation.D: Correct. Text 2's maze experiment shows the brain directing an arm step by step, which the claim that the brain issues "only broad commands" leaves out.
